scope: NetSuite reporting ledger, not payment processing or a concurrent refund authorization service
specApproval: Business rules confirmed in conversation; executable spec approval not obtained (autonomous run)
setup: New isolated SuiteScript bundle and node:test harness only. No application changes, commits, financial writes, new runtime dependencies, or production deployment. Reuse installed test-image dev tools if available. All tests run in disposable bounded containers through the retention runner.
scenarios: Cash 200 or 220, VISA 800, six pallets at net 40 and 13 percent tax => cash five at 40, VISA one at 45.20.
Multiple cash receipts combine within one invoice before flooring; amounts applied to other invoices and unapplied funds are excluded.
Different invoice lines, currencies, subsidiaries, payment methods, and last fours cannot lend funds to each other; original source IDs remain recorded.
Cash excludes tax; all other methods include actual line tax. Missing tax, fractional pallets, discounts, nonuniform per-unit amounts and unsupported transaction sources fail review.

Historical memo delimiters include parentheses, full-width parentheses, slash, plus, ideographic comma and hash after a real SO/invoice/credit/payment reference. Leading zeros survive. Order numbers, dates, money, phone numbers, conflicts and bare four-digit strings never become a card ID.
Missing/ambiguous card evidence marks the customer unverified. Original transaction memos are never rewritten.
Pure pallet credit plus exact applied Customer Refund amount can produce deterministic FIFO refund allocations with matching method/card/currency/subsidiary/rate and source before the credit date.
Mixed goods credits require explicit manual pallet refund allocations. Credits used on account, unmatched credits and incomplete historical provenance remain under review.
Pending manual allocation reserves once; completion replaces pending with refunded. Repeated reconciliation produces the same quantities and external IDs. Reversed entries do not consume pallets.
Manual allocations validate quantity, amount, credit limit, source scope and actual refund application; duplicate references, excess consumption and wrong-card refunds fail review.
Deposit Application traces to the original Customer Deposit, does not double count it, and checks source capacity. Unsupported deposit linkage fails review.

Customer physical balance from customsearch503 must equal invoice pallet quantity minus credit quantity before verified publication. Refund deductions are never subtracted again from that already-net physical search.
Dry run performs no custom-record writes. Only the two designated custom record types may be written; no financial record saves or deletes.

Only the designated single Map/Reduce deployment writes. Invalidate cached rows before rebuilding, reject changed source snapshots, stable external IDs prevent retry duplicates, and obsolete rows remain unverified.
Scheduled report has an explicit as-of time and is not a live reservation lock. A refund must be confirmed in NetSuite; a posted record alone is not proof of processor settlement.
additionalScenarios: Historical pallet credit already used against invoices can be manually marked APPLIED, with original funding selected and actual credit-application capacity verified; this consumes the refunded/settled counter without inventing a cash/card refund.
Consolidated invoice lines retain their own Sales Order and payments received after a historical return cannot finance that return.

Disposable development-only tools: TypeScript 5.9.3 (JS checks), ESLint 9.39.1 (complexity/lint), c8 10.1.3 (coverage), fast-check 4.3.0 (generated invariants). No dependencies are installed in the application or uploaded to NetSuite.

uploadHeaderCorrection.scope: Comment formatting correction only; retain SuiteScript 2.1 and all existing calculation and persistence behavior.
uploadHeaderCorrection.acceptance: All five upload files declare exactly one NApiVersion value of 2.1 on its own line inside a JSDoc block. Only ppa_rebuild_mr.js declares NScriptType MapReduceScript. NetSuite tag values extend to the next line break, so the closing comment delimiter must be on a separate line.
uploadHeaderCorrection.setup: Add a source-header regression check to the existing isolated suite and replace the download package. Reuse existing disposable tooling; no new dependencies, application edits, NetSuite writes or deployment.

repeatedUploadDiagnostic.status: Superseded: user confirmed successful v2 upload and native preview. The local CRLF diagnostic passed 48 acceptance tests but was not delivered or deployed; its temporary source helpers were removed.
repeatedUploadDiagnostic.scope: The user still reports an upload rejection after v2. Root cause remains unconfirmed; local checks are not NetSuite native validation.
repeatedUploadDiagnostic.acceptance: Export the five unchanged scripts as UTF-8 without BOM using CRLF. Normalizing CRLF back to LF must reproduce every source byte. Run the existing acceptance suite against the exported files. A separate zero-dependency Map/Reduce upload check returns an empty input list.
repeatedUploadDiagnostic.setup: Use Node standard-library tooling and the existing bounded disposable runner. Provide a distinct v3 download and individual diagnostic file. No financial record changes, NetSuite uploads or deployment are performed by these local steps.

failureModel.wrongCard: memo adversarial/property tests and exact method/card matching
failureModel.overAllocation: integer arithmetic, property tests, source/applied capacity checks
failureModel.partialWrite: fault-injected persistence boundary tests and invalidation
failureModel.staleOrConcurrent: single deployment, source recheck, cached-report limitation and dry-run first
failureModel.historicalGaps: unverified review output and physical search reconciliation
failureModel.secrets: no credentials in bundle; only read-only live diagnostics

v3Extension.scope: User-requested transaction-triggered refresh, truthful completion logs, full historical cash-credit quantity handling, and Cash summary grouping. Queue mutations are the sole addition to the original custom-record write allowlist.
